title: ZIP, Archive
documentation:
## File type
The concrete file format. Each value identifies a single, well-known format with its
file extensions and MIME type. File-type is the identity-tag of file-format media URNs:
`media:pdf` carries the pdf file-type marker, `media:json;textable;record` carries the
json file-type marker.

The file-type dim is authored across multiple fragment files in `fabric/dims/file-type/`
grouped by category (image, audio, video, archive, document, source, font, model,
data, config, web, other). Fragment merging produces a single global file-type dim
catalogue.

ZIP archive. Universal compressed container; multiple files bundled with per-entry
deflate compression.

## Medium
Medium tags declare the primary human-perceivable nature of a value: visual, audible,
textual, etc. Medium is what a person experiences when consuming the value. Some media
types carry multiple media tags (a PDF is both visual when displayed and textable when
its text layer is extracted).

Medium should not be confused with coercion: `textable` (coercion) means "can be
encoded as UTF-8 text without loss"; `textual` (medium) means "is fundamentally text
to a human reader." A JSON config is textable but not necessarily textual in this
sense — it is structured data that happens to be text-encoded.

The value is a compressed bundle of files (zip, tar.gz, 7z, etc.). Caps for archive
inspection or extraction match on this tag rather than on a specific archive format.

## Medium

title: Integer, List, Numeric, Textable
description: Numeric primitive (integer or real) optionally as a list
documentation:
## Number kind
Refines a numeric value with its number-system domain. A numeric value without a
number-kind tag is unconstrained on this axis. Adding a kind narrows what arithmetic
and comparison operations are well-defined on the value.

A whole number, positive, negative, or zero. No fractional part. Suitable for counts,
indices, ranks, and any quantity that cannot meaningfully take a decimal value.

## List marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is an ordered sequence at its
root: a JSON array, a multi-row CSV, a YAML sequence, a list of strings.
Independent of `record-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is an ordered sequence. Consumers can expect to iterate
elements in order.

## Numeric
Coercion marker indicating the value supports numeric operations (addition,
comparison, ordering). Independent of `textable`; a numeric value is often
also textable (an integer is encodable as text), but neither implies the
other in general.

The value supports numeric operations.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## File type
The concrete file format. Each value identifies a single, well-known format with its
file extensions and MIME type. File-type is the identity-tag of file-format media URNs:
`media:pdf` carries the pdf file-type marker, `media:json;textable;record` carries the
json file-type marker.

The file-type dim is authored across multiple fragment files in `fabric/dims/file-type/`
grouped by category (image, audio, video, archive, document, source, font, model,
data, config, web, other). Fragment merging produces a single global file-type dim
catalogue.

CSV (Comma-Separated Values). Tabular text format with field delimiter, RFC 4180
quoting rules.

## List marker

root: a JSON array, a multi-row CSV, a YAML sequence, a list of strings.

either alone, or neither.

The value's content is an ordered sequence. Consumers can expect to iterate
elements in order.

root: a JSON object, a CSV row with named columns, a TOML table, an INI file.
Independent of `list-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is a key-value mapping. Consumers can expect to address
fields by name.

Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Data format
The serialization format of structured data. A value tagged with both a data-format
and a structure tag tells consumers exactly how to parse the bytes into a structured
representation. JSON is the default for cap inter-step data exchange.

bifaci wire protocol for frame payloads.

## File type

TrueType font. Outline-font format originally developed by Apple.

## Medium
Medium tags declare the primary human-perceivable nature of a value: visual, audible,
textual, etc. Medium is what a person experiences when consuming the value. Some media
types carry multiple media tags (a PDF is both visual when displayed and textable when
its text layer is extracted).

Medium should not be confused with coercion: `textable` (coercion) means "can be
encoded as UTF-8 text without loss"; `textual` (medium) means "is fundamentally text
to a human reader." A JSON config is textable but not necessarily textual in this
sense — it is structured data that happens to be text-encoded.

The value is a font file (ttf, otf, woff, woff2). Caps for font inspection or
rendering match on this tag.

title: JSON, List, Record, Textable
documentation:
## Data format
The serialization format of structured data. A value tagged with both a data-format
and a structure tag tells consumers exactly how to parse the bytes into a structured
representation. JSON is the default for cap inter-step data exchange.

JavaScript Object Notation. Text-based, human-readable, ubiquitous. The default
serialization for structured cap inputs and outputs.

## List marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is an ordered sequence at its
root: a JSON array, a multi-row CSV, a YAML sequence, a list of strings.
Independent of `record-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is an ordered sequence. Consumers can expect to iterate
elements in order.

## Record marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is a key-value mapping at its
root: a JSON object, a CSV row with named columns, a TOML table, an INI file.
Independent of `list-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is a key-value mapping. Consumers can expect to address
fields by name.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

title: GLB, Model
documentation:
## File type
The concrete file format. Each value identifies a single, well-known format with its
file extensions and MIME type. File-type is the identity-tag of file-format media URNs:
`media:pdf` carries the pdf file-type marker, `media:json;textable;record` carries the
json file-type marker.

The file-type dim is authored across multiple fragment files in `fabric/dims/file-type/`
grouped by category (image, audio, video, archive, document, source, font, model,
data, config, web, other). Fragment merging produces a single global file-type dim
catalogue.

GLB binary glTF. Self-contained binary 3D model format.

## Medium
Medium tags declare the primary human-perceivable nature of a value: visual, audible,
textual, etc. Medium is what a person experiences when consuming the value. Some media
types carry multiple media tags (a PDF is both visual when displayed and textable when
its text layer is extracted).

Medium should not be confused with coercion: `textable` (coercion) means "can be
encoded as UTF-8 text without loss"; `textual` (medium) means "is fundamentally text
to a human reader." A JSON config is textable but not necessarily textual in this
sense — it is structured data that happens to be text-encoded.

coreml) or a 3D-mesh model file (obj, fbx, stl, glb, gltf). Caps for model loading
or inspection match on this tag.

title: NDJSON, Textable
documentation:
## Data format
The serialization format of structured data. A value tagged with both a data-format
and a structure tag tells consumers exactly how to parse the bytes into a structured
representation. JSON is the default for cap inter-step data exchange.

Newline-delimited JSON. Each line is a complete JSON value. Suited to streaming
contexts where consumers process records one at a time without loading the entire
sequence into memory.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

title: Record
description: Any value with key-value record structure
documentation:
## Record marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is a key-value mapping at its
root: a JSON object, a CSV row with named columns, a TOML table, an INI file.
Independent of `list-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is a key-value mapping. Consumers can expect to address
fields by name.

## Medium
Medium tags declare the primary human-perceivable nature of a value: visual, audible,
textual, etc. Medium is what a person experiences when consuming the value. Some media
types carry multiple media tags (a PDF is both visual when displayed and textable when

title: YAML, List, Record, Textable
documentation:
## Data format
The serialization format of structured data. A value tagged with both a data-format
and a structure tag tells consumers exactly how to parse the bytes into a structured
representation. JSON is the default for cap inter-step data exchange.

YAML Ain't Markup Language. Indentation-based, supports references and anchors.
Common for configuration and authoring contexts where humans edit files directly.

## List marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is an ordered sequence at its
root: a JSON array, a multi-row CSV, a YAML sequence, a list of strings.
Independent of `record-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is an ordered sequence. Consumers can expect to iterate
elements in order.

## Record marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is a key-value mapping at its
root: a JSON object, a CSV row with named columns, a TOML table, an INI file.
Independent of `list-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is a key-value mapping. Consumers can expect to address
fields by name.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

title: Adapter Selection Result (JSON, Record)
description: Set of media URNs identified by a cartridge content-inspection adapter
documentation:
## Purpose
Returned by a cartridge content-inspection adapter (`cap:in="media:";out="media:adapter-selection;json;record"`) to report which media URNs the adapter believes match the inspected file content. The orchestrator uses this to select the most specific matching URN or present choices when multiple URNs are returned.

## When to use
This media type is produced exclusively by adapter caps declared in cartridge cap groups. It is not intended for general use in pipelines.

## Schema
The payload is a JSON object with a single required field:

- `media_urns` — a non-empty array of media URN strings that the adapter is confident the file content matches.

When multiple URNs are returned, the orchestrator selects the most specific one (highest specificity score). If the array is empty or the adapter returns an empty END frame, the orchestrator falls back to extension-based lookup in the media spec registry.

## Example
A JSON adapter inspecting a file that starts with `[{` might return:
```json
{"media_urns": ["media:json;list;record;textable", "media:json;list;textable", "media:json;textable"]}
```
The orchestrator would pick `media:json;list;record;textable` as the most specific.

A simpler adapter that only identifies the family:
```json
{"media_urns": ["media:json;textable"]}
```

## Notes
The URNs returned must be URNs that exist in the media spec registry. The orchestrator validates each returned URN and discards any that are not registered. If all are discarded, it falls back to extension-based lookup.

## Data format
The serialization format of structured data. A value tagged with both a data-format
and a structure tag tells consumers exactly how to parse the bytes into a structured
representation. JSON is the default for cap inter-step data exchange.

JavaScript Object Notation. Text-based, human-readable, ubiquitous. The default
serialization for structured cap inputs and outputs.

## Record marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is a key-value mapping at its
root: a JSON object, a CSV row with named columns, a TOML table, an INI file.
Independent of `list-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is a key-value mapping. Consumers can expect to address
fields by name.

title: Cache Dir (Textable)
description: Cache Dir value
documentation:
## Purpose

Cache Dir specifies the filesystem path where the application stores cached data, including model artifacts, embeddings, and API response caches. Centralizing the cache directory simplifies backup and disk-space management.

## When to use

Set this when the default cache location (typically a platform-specific application data directory) is unsuitable, such as when a larger or faster disk is available at a different path. Relative paths are resolved from the application's working directory unless documented otherwise.

## Notes

The path must not contain null bytes. Ensure the process has read and write permission to the specified directory. Changing the cache directory does not migrate existing cached data; the new directory will be populated from scratch on first use.

documentation:
## Purpose
A boolean flag that controls whether a machine emits progress or result notifications to a registered callback endpoint during or after execution.

## When to use
Enable when a long-running machine should notify an external system of completion or intermediate results without requiring the caller to poll. Disable for synchronous, request-response pipelines where callbacks add unnecessary complexity.

## Notes
Callback endpoint configuration is managed separately from this flag. Enabling callbacks requires that the runtime supports the callback mechanism and that a valid endpoint is registered. See [Stream Flag](https://capdag.com/browse/media:stream-flag;textable) for token-level streaming as an alternative to callbacks.

title: Chunk Overlap (Textable, Numeric)
description: Chunk Overlap numeric value
documentation:
## Purpose
Defines the number of tokens or characters shared between consecutive chunks when splitting a document. Overlap preserves context at chunk boundaries, reducing the risk of information loss.

## When to use
Use alongside [Chunk Size](https://capdag.com/browse/media:chunk-size;textable;numeric) on any machine that segments documents. A typical overlap is 10–20% of the chunk size. Set to 0 when strict non-overlapping segments are required (e.g., when deduplication is critical).

## Notes
Valid range: 0–500. Overlap must be less than chunk size. Larger overlaps increase index size and redundancy, which can reduce retrieval precision in embedding-based search.

explicit transformation that may be lossy.

title: Chunk Size (Textable, Numeric)
description: Chunk Size numeric value
documentation:
## Purpose
Specifies the maximum number of tokens or characters in a single chunk when splitting documents for processing. Controls the granularity of content segmentation.

## When to use
Set this parameter on chunking or ingestion machines that split large documents before passing them to models with limited context windows. Smaller chunks increase retrieval precision; larger chunks preserve more context per segment.

## Notes
Valid range: 10–2000. Pair with [Chunk Overlap](https://capdag.com/browse/media:chunk-overlap;textable;numeric) to retain context across chunk boundaries, and with [Max Content Length](https://capdag.com/browse/media:max-content-length;textable;numeric) to ensure chunks fit within downstream limits.

title: Code Context
description: Code Context contextual information
documentation:
## Purpose

Code Context provides background information about the codebase, architecture, or existing code that a model should take into account when generating or analyzing code. It is a free-form text field with a generous character limit.

## When to use

Use this media type to pass snippets of existing code, file structure descriptions, API contracts, or other developer context to a code-focused node. Pair it with [Programming Language](https://capdag.com/browse/media:programming-language;textable) and [Coding Style](https://capdag.com/browse/media:coding-style;textable) for best results.

## Notes

The maximum length is 65,536 characters. Prioritize the most relevant context rather than including entire files, as excess context can reduce output quality.

title: Coding Style (Textable)
description: Coding Style value
documentation:
## Purpose

Coding Style describes the formatting conventions, naming rules, and stylistic preferences that generated or reviewed code should follow. It is a free-form text field, allowing project-specific style guides to be expressed in plain language.

## When to use

Use this media type when a code generation node should adhere to a particular house style, linter configuration, or team convention. It works alongside [Programming Language](https://capdag.com/browse/media:programming-language;textable) and [Code Context](https://capdag.com/browse/media:code-contextable).

## Notes

Keep style descriptions concise and actionable. Examples such as "use snake_case for variables", "prefer early returns", or "max line length 100" are more effective than vague directives.

## Purpose
A probability cutoff below which a machine's output is considered unreliable and should be suppressed, flagged, or sent to a fallback path. Typically used in classification or decision machines.

## When to use
Set a confidence threshold when downstream processes require a minimum certainty level. Results with scores below the threshold can be routed for human review or discarded. A common starting point is 0.7–0.9 for high-precision tasks.

## Notes
Valid range: 0.0–1.0. A threshold of 0.0 accepts all results; 1.0 requires perfect certainty and will suppress most output. Pair with [Decision](https://capdag.com/browse/media:decision;json;record;textable) or classification output types that carry probability scores.

title: Creative Context

## Purpose

Creative Context supplies background narrative, world-building details, character notes, or thematic constraints that ground a creative writing task. It is a large free-form text field allowing rich, multi-paragraph briefings.

## When to use

Use this media type when a generative writing node needs domain context beyond a simple prompt. It complements [Genre](https://capdag.com/browse/media:genre;textable), [Tone](https://capdag.com/browse/media:tone;textable), and [Creativity Level](https://capdag.com/browse/media:creativity-level;textable;numeric) by providing the substantive material the model should draw from.

The maximum length is 16,384 characters. Structure the context with clear sections (setting, characters, constraints) to help the model prioritize when the field is densely populated.

description: Creativity Level numeric value
documentation:
## Purpose

Creativity Level is a normalized float between 0.0 and 1.0 that controls how adventurous or conservative the model's output should be. Lower values favor predictability and accuracy; higher values favor novelty and variation.

## When to use

Use this media type when a creative writing or brainstorming node exposes a creativity dial to callers. Pair it with [Genre](https://capdag.com/browse/media:genre;textable), [Tone](https://capdag.com/browse/media:tone;textable), and [Creative Context](https://capdag.com/browse/media:creative-contextable) to fully parameterize creative output.

## Notes

This value maps conceptually to a model's temperature parameter but is expressed on a 0–1 scale regardless of the underlying model's native range. Values above 0.8 may produce less coherent output for structured tasks; reserve them for purely generative use cases.

Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.

string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

description: Exclude Pattern value
documentation:
## Purpose

Exclude Pattern specifies items that should be removed from a collection even if they match other selection criteria. It acts as a deny-list filter applied after inclusion rules.

## When to use

Use this media type together with [Include Pattern](https://capdag.com/browse/media:include-pattern;textable) and [Filter Pattern](https://capdag.com/browse/media:filter-pattern;textable) when a node supports a layered matching strategy. Exclude patterns are evaluated last, so they take precedence over include patterns.

## Notes

The pattern syntax is determined by the consuming node. A common convention is glob-style wildcards (e.g., `*.tmp`, `build/**`). Verify the node's documentation before relying on regular expression syntax.

## When to use
Use this type when a machine needs to read from or write to a specific file, rather than receiving content inline. Prefer inline content media types when the file is small and the path adds unnecessary indirection.

## Notes

## Purpose

## When to use

Use this media type when a node needs a caller-supplied pattern to narrow down a set of inputs, files, or results. Combine it with [Include Pattern](https://capdag.com/browse/media:include-pattern;textable) and [Exclude Pattern](https://capdag.com/browse/media:exclude-pattern;textable) for fine-grained control over what passes through.

## Notes

## Notes

description: Bearer token for the HuggingFace Hub API.
documentation:
## Purpose
Carries a HuggingFace Hub bearer token between caps. The token is forwarded as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to the HuggingFace API for the call's duration only — no implicit fallback to the `HF_TOKEN` environment variable, no global state.

## When to use
Use this media type for any cap argument that must reach gated HuggingFace repositories (license-protected models such as the `gemma-*` family). Caps that do not provide a token to a gated download fail hard with a clear authentication error.

## Notes
- The `secret` tag instructs UIs and logs to mask the value.
- An empty string is treated as "no token". Pass a non-empty string to authenticate.

## Security
Security tags annotate values with handling requirements. Values tagged `secret`
are treated as confidential — log redaction, masked display, and secure-channel
transport apply automatically.

description: Index Range value
documentation:
## Purpose
Specifies a numeric range of indices in the format `N` (single index) or `N-M` (inclusive range from N to M), used to select a subset of items from an ordered collection.

## When to use
Use this type to select pages, lines, chunks, or records by position. Supply `5` to select index 5 only, or `2-7` to select indices 2 through 7 inclusive.

## Notes
Pattern: `^\d+(-\d*)?$`. An open-ended range (e.g., `5-`) means "from index 5 to the end"; the machine must define this behavior. string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires

A sampling-strategy parameter for stochastic processes — most commonly LLM token
sampling (temperature, top-k, top-p, repeat penalty, seed).

## Settings audience
Who is expected to read or modify the setting. Audience determines which UI surface
exposes the setting (end-user preferences vs operator console vs developer tuning).

End-user preferences. Shown in the standard preferences UI. Safe defaults are chosen
to work for non-technical users; modifying these settings should not require
operational expertise.

## Settings scope
The lifecycle attachment of a setting value. App-scoped settings persist across
launches; task-scoped settings apply for the duration of a single cap or workflow
execution; model-scoped settings attach to a specific model artifact.

Applies for the duration of a single task or workflow run. May default from app
preferences but can be overridden per execution.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Numeric
Coercion marker indicating the value supports numeric operations (addition,
comparison, ordering). Independent of `textable`; a numeric value is often
also textable (an integer is encodable as text), but neither implies the
other in general.

The value supports numeric operations.

title: Inspection Depth (Textable)
description: Inspection Depth value
documentation:
## Purpose
A qualitative selector that controls how thoroughly a machine examines its input. The three levels (`summary`, `detailed`, `full`) trade off speed and token usage against completeness of analysis.

## When to use
Use `summary` for quick triage or routing decisions. Use `detailed` for standard analysis where most relevant content should be surfaced. Use `full` when exhaustive inspection is required, such as compliance review or deep extraction tasks.

## Notes
Allowed values: `summary`, `detailed`, `full`. For numeric depth control in hierarchical documents, use [Outline Max Depth](https://capdag.com/browse/media:outline-max-depth;textable;numeric). The computational cost typically scales with depth level.

The serialization format of structured data. A value tagged with both a data-format

Semantic-role markers distinguish how a value is used in a flow from how it is

routing decisions explicit.

title: Language Code (Textable)
description: Language Code value
documentation:
## Purpose
Carries a two-letter language code that machines use to tag or constrain content by language. Functionally equivalent to [Language](https://capdag.com/browse/media:language;textable) but signals explicit BCP 47 intent.

## When to use
Use this type when a machine port is documented to accept a language code rather than a free-text language name. Both types share the same validation set, so they are interchangeable in most graphs.

## Notes
Allowed values: `en`, `es`, `fr`, `de`, `it`, `pt`, `ru`, `zh`, `ja`, `ko`. For general language selection, [Language](https://capdag.com/browse/media:language;textable) is preferred unless the downstream machine specifically requires a coded value.

Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their

title: LLM Generation Request (JSON, Record)
description: Request object for LLM text generation containing prompt, model specification, and generation parameters
documentation:
## Purpose
Carries all inputs needed to invoke an LLM text generation cap: the prompt, the model to use, and any sampling or constraint parameters. A single request object lets callers express the full generation intent without needing multiple input ports.

## When to use
Pass this type to any cap that performs text generation, vocabulary inspection (`get_vocab`), or model information retrieval (`get_info`). For streaming responses the cap should produce a [LLM Text Stream](https://capdag.com/browse/media:llm-text-stream;ndjson); for batch responses it produces [Generated Text](https://capdag.com/browse/media:generated-text;textable;record).

## Notes
The `request_type` field defaults to `generate` when absent. Constraint fields (`grammar`, `json_schema`, `constraint`) are mutually exclusive in practice; implementers should apply the first one present. The `model_spec` value follows the same format described in [Model Spec](https://capdag.com/browse/media:model-spec;textable).

## Data format
The serialization format of structured data. A value tagged with both a data-format
and a structure tag tells consumers exactly how to parse the bytes into a structured
representation. JSON is the default for cap inter-step data exchange.

title: Generated Text (Textable, Record)
description: Generated text structured as a map with metadata.
documentation:
## Purpose
Carries the complete text generation result from an LLM cap, including the generated text and any associated metadata such as token counts, finish reason, and timing. This is the non-streaming counterpart to [LLM Text Stream](https://capdag.com/browse/media:llm-text-stream;ndjson).

## When to use
Use this type when a cap returns the full generated output in one shot rather than streaming tokens. Callers that do not need incremental delivery should prefer this simpler interface over the streaming variant.

## Notes
The outer object is a flat map; implementations should include at minimum a `text` or `generated_text` key containing the model output. Additional metadata keys such as `tokens_generated`, `finish_reason`, and `generation_time_ms` are recommended for observability.

title: LLM Model Info (JSON, Record)
description: Information about a loaded LLM model including capabilities and parameters
documentation:
## Purpose
Describes a loaded LLM's structural properties and capabilities, including vocabulary size, maximum context length, embedding dimensions, and feature flags such as chat template and tool-use support.

## When to use
Retrieve this type when a cap or orchestrator needs to know model capabilities before issuing a generation request. It is the response to a `get_info` request in a [LLM Generation Request](https://capdag.com/browse/media:llm-generation-request;json;record).

## Notes
The `model_spec` and `vocab_size` fields are required. All other fields are optional and may be absent if the model file does not expose the corresponding metadata. Callers should treat missing fields as unknown rather than assuming a default value.

## Data format
The serialization format of structured data. A value tagged with both a data-format
and a structure tag tells consumers exactly how to parse the bytes into a structured
representation. JSON is the default for cap inter-step data exchange.

title: LLM Text Stream (NDJSON)
description: Streaming output from LLM text generation. Each line is a JSON object with a 'type' field (token, status, complete, tool_request, or error).
documentation:
## Purpose
Provides incremental LLM output as newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON). Each line is a self-contained JSON object that consumers can parse and act on as tokens arrive, without waiting for the full response.

## When to use
Use this type for interactive or latency-sensitive applications where displaying tokens as they are generated improves perceived responsiveness. The final `complete` message signals end of stream and carries aggregate statistics. For non-interactive use, prefer [Generated Text](https://capdag.com/browse/media:generated-text;textable;record).

## Notes
The `type` discriminator is required on every message. Consumers must handle all five types: `token` (partial text), `status` (progress update), `complete` (final summary), `tool_request` (the model wants to invoke a tool), and `error` (generation failed). Messages of unknown type should be silently skipped to allow forward compatibility.

## Data format
The serialization format of structured data. A value tagged with both a data-format
and a structure tag tells consumers exactly how to parse the bytes into a structured
representation. JSON is the default for cap inter-step data exchange.

Newline-delimited JSON. Each line is a complete JSON value. Suited to streaming
contexts where consumers process records one at a time without loading the entire
sequence into memory.

title: LLM Vocabulary Response (JSON, Record)
description: Response containing the model's vocabulary tokens
documentation:
## Purpose
Returns the full token vocabulary of a loaded LLM, enabling token-level analysis, prompt engineering tools, and custom tokenization utilities to operate without a separate tokenizer library.

## When to use
This is the response to a `get_vocab` request in a [LLM Generation Request](https://capdag.com/browse/media:llm-generation-request;json;record). Use it when you need to enumerate, inspect, or count the tokens the model recognises.

## Notes
The `vocab` array is ordered by token ID. The `vocab_size` field should equal the length of `vocab`; include it as a convenience for consumers that only need the count without iterating the full array. Vocabulary extraction is typically slow on large models; cache the result when possible.

## Data format
The serialization format of structured data. A value tagged with both a data-format
and a structure tag tells consumers exactly how to parse the bytes into a structured
representation. JSON is the default for cap inter-step data exchange.

title: Max Content Length (Textable, Numeric)
description: Max Content Length numeric value
documentation:
## Purpose
Limits the number of characters or tokens of document content passed to a machine. Used to prevent oversized inputs from exceeding downstream capacity.

## When to use
Apply this parameter on ingestion or preprocessing machines that must truncate or split content before forwarding it. It complements [Max Context Length](https://capdag.com/browse/media:max-context-length;inference;limit;operator;model;textable;numeric), which governs the model's total window.

## Notes
Valid range: 256–131072. Content exceeding this limit should be chunked using [Chunk Size](https://capdag.com/browse/media:chunk-size;textable;numeric) rather than silently truncated.

description: Mlx Model Path file system path
documentation:
## Purpose
Carries the local filesystem path to an MLX-format model directory on Apple Silicon. MLX models have a specific directory layout that differs from GGUF or safetensors formats, so a dedicated type allows caps to route MLX-specific paths without ambiguity.

## When to use
Use this type when passing a model path between caps that are specifically designed for the MLX backend, such as an MLX download cap and an MLX inference cap. For backend-agnostic path passing use [Model Path](https://capdag.com/browse/media:model-path;textable;record).

## Notes
The path must be non-empty (min_length = 1). The directory at this path must conform to the MLX model layout expected by the target cap. This type is only meaningful on macOS with Apple Silicon; on other platforms the MLX backend is unavailable.

## Textable

## Purpose
Carries the set of architecture identifiers a cap supports (its `supported_model_types`). Used by `list-compatible-models` and similar caps to drive cap-aware model pickers — the user is presented only with models whose detected architecture is in this set.

## When to use
Pass this record from a cap's `supported_model_types` declaration to `cap:op=list-compatible-models` to retrieve the cached models the cap can run. The same shape is reused by the `architectures` field of `media:model-search-request`.

## Notes
Architecture identifiers are HuggingFace `config.json` `model_type` values (e.g. `mistral`, `llama`, `qwen2`, `phi3`, `gemma2`). They are NOT pipeline tags — `text-generation` is a pipeline tag, not an architecture.

## Data format
The serialization format of structured data. A value tagged with both a data-format
and a structure tag tells consumers exactly how to parse the bytes into a structured
representation. JSON is the default for cap inter-step data exchange.

documentation:
## Purpose
Answers whether a given model is present on the local filesystem and whether it exists in its source repository. This is the lightweight check a cap can perform before deciding whether to download, load, or surface a model to the user.

## When to use
Use this type as the output of an availability-check cap when you need a simple yes/no answer before committing to a full download or load operation. For richer per-file inventory use [Model Contents](https://capdag.com/browse/media:model-contents;textable;record); for download progress use [Model Status](https://capdag.com/browse/media:model-status;textable;record).

## Notes
`local_available` and `remote_available` are both required. The `local_path` and `size_bytes` fields are optional and populated only when the model is locally present. The `last_modified` timestamp follows ISO 8601 and reflects the local file's modification time.

## Purpose

## Number kind

and comparison operations are well-defined on the value.

## Purpose

## When to use
Use this type as the output of any cap that lists models, whether filtered by type, availability, or other criteria. ## Notes
The `path` field is required. The `exists` flag allows callers to distinguish between a path that was computed but not yet downloaded versus one that is on disk and ready to use. Use [Model Availability](https://capdag.com/browse/media:model-availability;textable;record) when you need both local and remote availability in one response.

description: JSON record carrying a remote-model search query, optionally restricted by architecture.
documentation:
## Purpose

title: Model Spec (Textable, GGUF (llama.cpp), LLM, Mistral)
description: Model specification (scheme:identifier string identifying a machine-learning model).
documentation:
## Purpose
A model spec is a compact string that uniquely identifies a machine learning model
and tells the system where to find it. The format is `<scheme>:<identifier>` with
an optional query string for filtering (e.g. `hf:org/model-name?include=*Q8_0*`).
The scheme determines which backend or repository resolves the spec.

## Tag axes
The base anchor `model-spec` may be specialised along three orthogonal axes:
backend (gguf / mlx / candle), model-task (llm / vision / embeddings /
image-embeddings / transcription), and family (mistral / llama / phi / qwen).
Backend-agnostic specs simply omit the backend tag.

## Notes
The validation regex requires the scheme separator colon to be present and forbids
embedded whitespace in the identifier. Strings of up to 512 characters are allowed
to accommodate long query strings.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Backend
The inference framework or runtime that loads and executes a model. Backend choice
determines weight format, hardware acceleration, and runtime characteristics. A media
URN that omits the backend tag is backend-agnostic — it accepts any backend.

GGUF is the llama.cpp container format. Quantised weights packaged into a single
file with embedded metadata. Runs efficiently on CPU and via Metal/CUDA acceleration.
Standard format for general-purpose LLM and embedding inference across hardware.

## Model task
The inference modality of a model. Model-task narrows what kind of inference cap a
model spec is suitable for: an LLM cannot serve transcription, a transcription model
cannot serve text generation. The task tag is part of the model-spec URN; it is set
by the cap declaring its model-spec input slot, not derived from the model file.

Causal language model for text generation and instruction following. Accepts a text
prompt and produces a text continuation, typically token-by-token via streaming.

## Family
The model family — its architectural lineage. Families share chat templates, tokenizer
configurations, and structural assumptions. The runtime applies family-specific prompt
formatting (e.g. `[INST]/[/INST]` for Mistral, header_id for Llama 3) when invoking
inference. Family is detected from the model spec by content inspection.

Mistral and Mixtral family. Uses the `[INST]/[/INST]` chat template. Includes
Mistral-7B, Mistral-Nemo, Mixtral-8x7B and derivatives.

A model spec is a compact string that uniquely identifies a machine learning model
and tells the system where to find it. The format is `<scheme>:<identifier>` with
an optional query string for filtering (e.g. `hf:org/model-name?include=*Q8_0*`).
The scheme determines which backend or repository resolves the spec.

## Tag axes
The base anchor `model-spec` may be specialised along three orthogonal axes:
backend (gguf / mlx / candle), model-task (llm / vision / embeddings /
image-embeddings / transcription), and family (mistral / llama / phi / qwen).
Backend-agnostic specs simply omit the backend tag.

## Notes
The validation regex requires the scheme separator colon to be present and forbids
embedded whitespace in the identifier. Strings of up to 512 characters are allowed
to accommodate long query strings.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Backend
The inference framework or runtime that loads and executes a model. Backend choice
determines weight format, hardware acceleration, and runtime characteristics. A media
URN that omits the backend tag is backend-agnostic — it accepts any backend.

GGUF is the llama.cpp container format. Quantised weights packaged into a single
file with embedded metadata. Runs efficiently on CPU and via Metal/CUDA acceleration.
Standard format for general-purpose LLM and embedding inference across hardware.

## Model task
The inference modality of a model. Model-task narrows what kind of inference cap a
model spec is suitable for: an LLM cannot serve transcription, a transcription model
cannot serve text generation. The task tag is part of the model-spec URN; it is set
by the cap declaring its model-spec input slot, not derived from the model file.

Vision-language model for image captioning, visual question answering, and other
multimodal tasks. Accepts text and images, produces text.

title: Model Spec (Textable, MLX (Apple Silicon), Mistral)
description: Model specification (scheme:identifier string identifying a machine-learning model).
documentation:
## Purpose
A model spec is a compact string that uniquely identifies a machine learning model
and tells the system where to find it. The format is `<scheme>:<identifier>` with
an optional query string for filtering (e.g. `hf:org/model-name?include=*Q8_0*`).
The scheme determines which backend or repository resolves the spec.

## Tag axes
The base anchor `model-spec` may be specialised along three orthogonal axes:
backend (gguf / mlx / candle), model-task (llm / vision / embeddings /
image-embeddings / transcription), and family (mistral / llama / phi / qwen).
Backend-agnostic specs simply omit the backend tag.

## Notes
The validation regex requires the scheme separator colon to be present and forbids
embedded whitespace in the identifier. Strings of up to 512 characters are allowed
to accommodate long query strings.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Backend
The inference framework or runtime that loads and executes a model. Backend choice
determines weight format, hardware acceleration, and runtime characteristics. A media
URN that omits the backend tag is backend-agnostic — it accepts any backend.

MLX is Apple's array framework for machine learning, native to Apple Silicon. Models
are stored as safetensors with MLX-specific config. Exploits the unified memory
architecture of M-series chips for fast, energy-efficient inference. Apple Silicon
only.

## Family
The model family — its architectural lineage. Families share chat templates, tokenizer
configurations, and structural assumptions. The runtime applies family-specific prompt
formatting (e.g. `[INST]/[/INST]` for Mistral, header_id for Llama 3) when invoking
inference. Family is detected from the model spec by content inspection.

Mistral and Mixtral family. Uses the `[INST]/[/INST]` chat template. Includes
Mistral-7B, Mistral-Nemo, Mixtral-8x7B and derivatives.

A model spec is a compact string that uniquely identifies a machine learning model
and tells the system where to find it. The format is `<scheme>:<identifier>` with
an optional query string for filtering (e.g. `hf:org/model-name?include=*Q8_0*`).
The scheme determines which backend or repository resolves the spec.

## Tag axes
The base anchor `model-spec` may be specialised along three orthogonal axes:
backend (gguf / mlx / candle), model-task (llm / vision / embeddings /
image-embeddings / transcription), and family (mistral / llama / phi / qwen).
Backend-agnostic specs simply omit the backend tag.

## Notes
The validation regex requires the scheme separator colon to be present and forbids
embedded whitespace in the identifier. Strings of up to 512 characters are allowed
to accommodate long query strings.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Backend
The inference framework or runtime that loads and executes a model. Backend choice
determines weight format, hardware acceleration, and runtime characteristics. A media
URN that omits the backend tag is backend-agnostic — it accepts any backend.

Candle is a lightweight Rust-based ML framework. Loads models in safetensors format
directly on CPU, Metal, or CUDA. Embeddable in Rust applications without Python
runtime overhead.

## Model task
The inference modality of a model. Model-task narrows what kind of inference cap a
model spec is suitable for: an LLM cannot serve transcription, a transcription model
cannot serve text generation. The task tag is part of the model-spec URN; it is set
by the cap declaring its model-spec input slot, not derived from the model file.

Vision-language model for image captioning, visual question answering, and other
multimodal tasks. Accepts text and images, produces text.

## Family
The model family — its architectural lineage. Families share chat templates, tokenizer
configurations, and structural assumptions. The runtime applies family-specific prompt
formatting (e.g. `[INST]/[/INST]` for Mistral, header_id for Llama 3) when invoking
inference. Family is detected from the model spec by content inspection.

Microsoft's Phi family (Phi-2, Phi-3, Phi-3.5). Uses `<|user|>` / `<|end|>` chat
template. Compact (1B–7B parameters) models optimised for reasoning tasks.

title: Model Spec (Textable, Transcription, Llama)
description: Model specification (scheme:identifier string identifying a machine-learning model).
documentation:
## Purpose
A model spec is a compact string that uniquely identifies a machine learning model
and tells the system where to find it. The format is `<scheme>:<identifier>` with
an optional query string for filtering (e.g. `hf:org/model-name?include=*Q8_0*`).
The scheme determines which backend or repository resolves the spec.

## Tag axes
The base anchor `model-spec` may be specialised along three orthogonal axes:
backend (gguf / mlx / candle), model-task (llm / vision / embeddings /
image-embeddings / transcription), and family (mistral / llama / phi / qwen).
Backend-agnostic specs simply omit the backend tag.

## Notes
The validation regex requires the scheme separator colon to be present and forbids
embedded whitespace in the identifier. Strings of up to 512 characters are allowed
to accommodate long query strings.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Model task
The inference modality of a model. Model-task narrows what kind of inference cap a
model spec is suitable for: an LLM cannot serve transcription, a transcription model
cannot serve text generation. The task tag is part of the model-spec URN; it is set
by the cap declaring its model-spec input slot, not derived from the model file.

Speech-to-text model (e.g. Whisper). Accepts audio, produces text transcription with
optional timestamps and speaker attribution.

## Family
The model family — its architectural lineage. Families share chat templates, tokenizer
configurations, and structural assumptions. The runtime applies family-specific prompt
formatting (e.g. `[INST]/[/INST]` for Mistral, header_id for Llama 3) when invoking
inference. Family is detected from the model spec by content inspection.

Meta's Llama family. Uses `<|header_id|>` / `<|eot_id|>` chat template (Llama 3).
Llama 2 uses an older `[INST]` template — the runtime detects exact variant from
the model's tokenizer config.

title: Model Status (Textable, Record)
description: Detailed model status including state, download progress, and health information
documentation:
## Purpose
Reports the lifecycle state of a model including whether it is not yet downloaded, actively downloading, paused, ready for use, or in an error state. When a download is in progress it also carries progress metrics such as bytes transferred and estimated time remaining.

## When to use
Poll or stream this type from a model management cap to track download or loading progress. UIs and orchestrators can use the `state` field to drive state machines and display progress bars, and inspect `error_message` on failure.

## Notes
The `state` field is required. Progress fields (`downloaded_bytes`, `total_bytes`, `progress`, `speed_bps`, `eta_seconds`) are only meaningful when `state` is `downloading`. The `local_path` field is populated once the model reaches the `ready` state. See [Model Availability](https://capdag.com/browse/media:model-availability;textable;record) for a simpler availability snapshot.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Record marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is a key-value mapping at its
root: a JSON object, a CSV row with named columns, a TOML table, an INI file.
Independent of `list-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is a key-value mapping. Consumers can expect to address
fields by name.

## Purpose
Limits how many levels deep a machine traverses when extracting or generating a document outline or hierarchical structure.

## When to use
Set this parameter on outline extraction, table-of-contents generation, or tree-traversal machines to control output granularity. A depth of 1 returns only top-level headings; higher values include nested subsections.

## Notes
Valid range: 1–10. A depth of 1 is the shallowest (top-level only). Deep outlines may be large; balance depth against the token budget of downstream machines. See [Inspection Depth](https://capdag.com/browse/media:inspection-depth;textable) for a qualitative depth control.

## Purpose
Specifies the pixel height to use when rendering a document page as an image. Controls the vertical resolution of the rasterized output.

title: plist, Record
documentation:
## File type
The concrete file format. Each value identifies a single, well-known format with its
file extensions and MIME type. File-type is the identity-tag of file-format media URNs:
`media:pdf` carries the pdf file-type marker, `media:json;textable;record` carries the
json file-type marker.

The file-type dim is authored across multiple fragment files in `fabric/dims/file-type/`
grouped by category (image, audio, video, archive, document, source, font, model,
data, config, web, other). Fragment merging produces a single global file-type dim
catalogue.

Apple property list. XML or binary key-value structure used throughout macOS / iOS.

## Record marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is a key-value mapping at its
root: a JSON object, a CSV row with named columns, a TOML table, an INI file.
Independent of `list-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is a key-value mapping. Consumers can expect to address
fields by name.

## Purpose
Specifies the numeric precision used when loading or running a model. Controls the trade-off between computation speed, memory usage, and output quality.

## When to use
Set this parameter when deploying models to hardware with specific memory constraints or when optimizing for inference throughput. `float32` offers maximum accuracy; `int4` offers maximum compression with some quality loss.

## Notes
Allowed values: `float32`, `float16`, `int8`, `int4`. Not all models support all precision levels; check the target model's quantization support. Lower precision reduces VRAM usage and increases throughput but may introduce rounding artifacts in sensitive tasks.

## Purpose
A boolean flag that prevents a machine from discarding any input data during transformation, summarization, or extraction. When enabled, all source content is carried through to the output.

## When to use
Enable when data loss is unacceptable, such as in archival workflows, compliance processing, or when a downstream machine requires the full original content alongside derived results.

## Notes
Enabling this flag typically increases output size and may conflict with token-limit or size constraints. See [Preserve Structure Flag](https://capdag.com/browse/media:preserve-structure-flag;textable) for a related flag that preserves document structure without necessarily retaining all content.

## Notes

## Purpose

## Notes

documentation:
## Purpose

Reasoning Context supplies background knowledge, constraints, or domain rules that a model should apply when performing logical analysis, question answering, or multi-step reasoning tasks.

## When to use

Use this media type when a reasoning or QA node needs grounding beyond its training knowledge. It is particularly valuable for specialized domains such as legal, scientific, or proprietary business logic where the model cannot be expected to reason correctly without explicit context.

## Notes

The maximum length is 32,768 characters, the largest of the context media types, reflecting the depth of background that complex reasoning tasks may require. Organize the context with numbered facts or labeled sections to help the model reference specific points in its output.

## Notes
The definition of "boilerplate" is machine-specific. See [Include Comments Flag](https://capdag.com/browse/media:include-comments-flag;textable) for the analogous control over code comments and [Preserve Structure Flag](https://capdag.com/browse/media:preserve-structure-flag;textable) for retaining document structure.

## Purpose

Use this media type when a node that loads models needs to know where to retrieve the artifact. Set to `huggingface` for models hosted on Hugging Face Hub, `local` for models already present on disk, and `custom` for any other registry accessible via the node's configuration.

## Notes

description: Schema Variables object with key-value pairs
documentation:
## Purpose

Schema Variables carry a JSON object of key-value pairs that are injected into a schema before validation or generation. They allow schemas to be templated and reused across different contexts by varying only the variable bindings.

## When to use

Use this media type when a node consumes a parameterized schema and needs the variable bindings resolved at runtime. It is similar in structure to [Substitutions](https://capdag.com/browse/media:substitutions;textable;record) but scoped specifically to schema processing.

## Notes

Variable names should match the placeholder tokens defined in the schema. Unresolved variables may cause validation failures, so ensure all required keys are present before passing this value downstream.

## Purpose
An unsigned integer used to initialize the random number generator, making model outputs reproducible across runs when all other parameters are held constant.

## Purpose
Carries the URN of the media type that was used as the source or input for a derived artifact. Provides provenance information so downstream machines and users can trace what kind of content originated the current output.

## When to use
Attach this value to output records from conversion, extraction, or transformation machines where consumers need to know the original media type. It is particularly useful in multi-modal pipelines that accept several input formats.

## Notes
Must match the pattern `^media:.+` with a minimum length of 7. The value should be a valid URN from the capdag media registry. See [File Path](https://capdag.com/browse/media:file-path;textable) for carrying the source file location alongside this URN.

documentation:
## File type
The concrete file format. Each value identifies a single, well-known format with its
file extensions and MIME type. File-type is the identity-tag of file-format media URNs:

json file-type marker.

The file-type dim is authored across multiple fragment files in `fabric/dims/file-type/`
grouped by category (image, audio, video, archive, document, source, font, model,
data, config, web, other). Fragment merging produces a single global file-type dim
catalogue.

description: Stream Flag value
documentation:
## Purpose
A boolean flag that instructs a machine to emit output incrementally as tokens are generated, rather than buffering the complete response before returning it.

## When to use
Enable streaming for user-facing interfaces where progressive display improves perceived responsiveness. Disable it (the default) for batch pipelines, post-processing chains, or any consumer that requires the full output before proceeding.

## Notes
Streaming behavior is transport-dependent. Not all machine hosts or output ports support streaming; check the runtime documentation. When streaming is enabled, intermediate output frames may not conform to the final content type's schema.

## Purpose

Substitutions carry a JSON object whose keys and values are plain strings. They are used to fill template placeholders in queries, prompts, or other parameterized content before execution.

## When to use

Use this media type when a node needs to receive a dynamic set of variable bindings at runtime. Pair it with [Query Name](https://capdag.com/browse/media:query-name;textable) to identify the query to execute and supply the values that replace its placeholders.

## Notes

Keys and values must both be strings. Nesting is not supported; flatten complex structures into dot-separated or underscore-separated key names before passing them as substitutions.

title: Summary Context
description: Summary Context contextual information
documentation:
## Purpose

Summary Context provides framing information that helps the model produce a more targeted summary, such as the intended audience, the reason for the summary, or key terms to prioritize.

## When to use

Use this media type alongside [Summary Type](https://capdag.com/browse/media:summary-type;textable) and [Summary Focus](https://capdag.com/browse/media:summary-focus;textable) when the summarization task requires audience-awareness or domain framing beyond what the source document itself provides.

## Notes

The maximum length is 8,192 characters. Brief, well-structured context (two to four sentences) is typically more effective than long narrative instructions.

title: Summary Focus (Textable)
description: Summary Focus value
documentation:
## Purpose

Summary Focus narrows the aspect of the source material that the summary should emphasize, ensuring the model highlights the information most relevant to the reader's purpose.

## When to use

Use this media type alongside [Summary Type](https://capdag.com/browse/media:summary-type;textable) when the summarization node supports focused extraction. For general-purpose summaries, `main_points` or `overview` are safe defaults.

## Notes

Choosing `methodology` or `results` is most effective for research documents. `implications` suits strategic or analytical content. When the source does not contain the chosen focus area, the model will fall back to available material and may not produce the expected structure.

## Textable

Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

title: Summary Type (Textable)
description: Summary Type value
documentation:
## Purpose

Summary Type selects the structural approach the model uses when condensing content. The choice affects both the form of the output (prose vs. bullets) and the level of interpretation applied (extractive vs. abstractive).

## When to use

Use this media type as an input to summarization nodes. Combine it with [Summary Focus](https://capdag.com/browse/media:summary-focus;textable) to specify both the method and the aspect of the source material to emphasize, and with [Summary Context](https://capdag.com/browse/media:summary-contextable) to provide framing information.

## Notes

`extractive` summaries quote directly from the source; `abstractive` ones rephrase in the model's own words. `executive` and `brief` are length-oriented presets, while `bullet_points` imposes a list structure regardless of length.

## Textable

Use this media type when a machine port accepts a session-level instruction block that governs all subsequent turns. description: Timestamps Flag value
documentation:
## Purpose
A boolean flag that instructs a machine to annotate its output with timestamps, typically indicating when each segment was produced or what time range it corresponds to.

## When to use
Enable for audio transcription, log processing, or time-series analysis machines where temporal anchoring of output segments is required. Disable when timestamps would clutter or complicate downstream parsing.

## Notes
See also [Timestamps](https://capdag.com/browse/media:timestamps;textable), which carries timestamp data as a media value rather than as a flag controlling output behavior. Timestamp format is machine-specific.

title: Timestamps (Textable)
description: Boolean flag indicating whether to include timestamps in output.
documentation:
## Purpose
Carries a boolean value indicating whether the receiving machine should include timestamps in its output. Serves as a data-carrying counterpart to the behavioral [Timestamps Flag](https://capdag.com/browse/media:timestamps-flag;textable).

## When to use
Use this type when a graph passes a timestamps preference as a data value between machines rather than as a static configuration. For static configuration, prefer [Timestamps Flag](https://capdag.com/browse/media:timestamps-flag;textable).

## Notes
The exact interpretation of "timestamps" (segment start/end times, wall-clock annotations, etc.) is determined by the downstream machine. Ensure the receiving machine documents its timestamp format.

## Textable

Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

title: Tone (Textable)
description: Tone value
documentation:
## Purpose

Tone specifies the emotional register and interpersonal stance of the generated text, shaping how readers experience the content rather than what information it conveys.

## When to use

Use this media type alongside [Genre](https://capdag.com/browse/media:genre;textable) and [Creativity Level](https://capdag.com/browse/media:creativity-level;textable;numeric) when configuring creative or editorial writing nodes. It is also applicable to customer-facing content nodes where brand voice matters.

## Notes

Tone affects word choice, sentence rhythm, and the degree of formality. When tone and genre conflict (for example, `humorous` with `academic`), the model will attempt to honor both, but results may vary; test outputs carefully.

## Textable

Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

## File type
The concrete file format. Each value identifies a single, well-known format with its
file extensions and MIME type. File-type is the identity-tag of file-format media URNs:
`media:pdf` carries the pdf file-type marker, `media:json;textable;record` carries the

The file-type dim is authored across multiple fragment files in `fabric/dims/file-type/`
grouped by category (image, audio, video, archive, document, source, font, model,
data, config, web, other). Fragment merging produces a single global file-type dim
catalogue.

vCard. Contact-card interchange format.

## List marker

root: a JSON array, a multi-row CSV, a YAML sequence, a list of strings.
Independent of `record-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is an ordered sequence. Consumers can expect to iterate

title: Void Value
description: No value / void return type
documentation:
## Purpose
The [Void Value](https://capdag.com/browse/media:void) media type represents the absence of a value — analogous to `void` in programming languages or `null` in type theory. It is used to type ports or outputs that carry no data payload.

## When to use
Use this type for node outputs that signal completion or success without returning any data — for example, a side-effectful node that writes to a database and has nothing to return, or a terminal sink node. It is also appropriate as the type of an optional input port whose absence is meaningful.

## Notes
A void value produces no bytes; its byte length is always zero. Implementers should not transmit any payload when producing a void value, and consumers should ignore any payload bytes if present. This type is intentionally distinct from an empty byte sequence (`media:`) to make the semantic "no output" explicit in the graph schema.
